name: Bahraini Citizenship by Naturalisation (Bahraini Citizenship Act 1963, as amended)

requirements.blocker_text: 15 consecutive years of legal residence for Arab nationals, plus good conduct, Arabic language proficiency, and ownership of registered real estate in Bahrain.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 15 years of continuous legal residence.

requirements.blocker_text: 25 consecutive years of legal residence for non-Arab nationals, plus good conduct, Arabic language proficiency, and ownership of registered real estate in Bahrain.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 25 years of continuous legal residence.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 15 (or 25) years' continuous legal residence
Registered real estate ownership in Bahrain

sources.title: GLOBALCIT (EUI academic citizenship-law observatory) -- English translation of the Bahraini Citizenship Act 1963, as amended: 15-year residence requirement for Arab nationals, 25 years for non-Arab nationals, plus good conduct, Arabic proficiency, and real-estate ownership

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bahrain). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to GLOBALCIT, an academic legal-text database hosting a translation of the primary statute (treated as tier 2, consistent with this dataset's convention for academic/research hosts of verbatim government legal text -- see Qatar's and Moldova's citizenship files for the same treatment). Bahrain's own Legislation portal (legalaffairs.gov.bh) was not directly queried in this build -- recommend cross-checking there for the authoritative Arabic/official text before upgrading this file to published. DISTINCTIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING, CONFIRMED: Bahrain draws an explicit ARAB/NON-ARAB distinction in ordinary naturalisation residence requirements -- 15 years vs. 25 years -- a nationality-based (not merely country-of-origin) two-tier system not seen structured quite this way elsewhere in this dataset. A registered real-estate ownership requirement, on top of years of residence and language proficiency, is also a distinctive add-on. dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE -- see bh_citizenship_special_grounds.json's revocation provisions, under which voluntarily acquiring a second nationality can trigger loss of Bahraini citizenship by Governor's order, unlike several other Gulf states in this dataset that now permit dual nationality outright.
